For each real $\beta\in(-1,1)$ put $x':=B(\beta e_1)\circ x$ and $f_a:=B(\beta e_1)^{-1}e_a$; by [F5] the map $B(\beta e_1)$ is proper orthochronous with inverse $B(-\beta e_1)$, and [F5] applied to $-\beta e_1$ gives that $B(-\beta e_1)$ also preserves $\eta$, the future cone and the orientation, so the ordered basis $(f_0,f_1,f_2,f_3)=(B(-\beta e_1)e_0,\dots,B(-\beta e_1)e_3)$ is again $\eta$-orthonormal, future and positively oriented and $(o;f_0,f_1,f_2,f_3)$ is an inertial frame by [F6]; its chart is $x'$, because the frame isomorphism $E_f=E\circ B(\beta e_1)^{-1}$ gives $E_f^{-1}(p-o)=B(\beta e_1)(E^{-1}(p-o))=x'(p)$, and $f_0$ is future unit timelike. covariant components of the **electromagnetic two-form** $F$ in the chart by
$F_{00}=0$, $F_{0i}:=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}:=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$
($i,j,k\in\{1,2,3\}$) and $F_{ab}:=-F_{ba}$, the index-raised components being
$F^{0i}=E_i/c$, $F^{i0}=-E_i/c$ and $F^{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$. Here
$\epsilon_{ijk}$ is the spatial permutation symbol of
[[def-oriented-minkowski-volume-form]]. Then $F$ is a $C^k$ type-$(0,2)$
tensor field on $U$ in the sense of
[[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]], alternating at every event, and the
components above are exactly its component functions: at $p\in U$ the tensor
$F(p)$ is the bilinear form $F(p)(u,w)=F_{ab}(p)u^aw^b$ on $V$ in the
coordinates $u^a,w^b$ of $u,w$ in $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$. Indeed each $F_{ab}$ is
a finite sum of products of the $C^k$ functions $E_i,B_k$ of the chart
coordinates with the constants $c,\epsilon_{ijk}$, hence a $C^k$ function of
$x(p)$, and the component criterion of
[[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]] applies.

(b) [Observer decomposition] Let $n:=e_0$ be the future unit timelike vector of
the chart and let $e_a:=F_{ab}n^b$, $b_a:=(*F)_{ab}n^b$ be the observer
components of [[thm-sr-antisymmetric-observer-decomposition]]; then
$e_i=+E_i/c$, $b_i=-B_i$ and $e_0=b_0=0$, and the invariants and square wedge
of that theorem read

$E=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$ and $B=\operatorname{curl}A$, and
$A^\mu:=(\varphi/c,A)$, $A_\mu:=\eta_{\mu\nu}A^\nu$, then
$F_{\mu\nu}=\partial_\mu A_\nu-\partial_\nu A_\mu$; conversely, if a $C^1$
covector field $A_\mu$ on $U$ satisfies $F_{\mu\nu}=\partial_\mu A_\nu
-\partial_\nu A_\mu$, then $E,B$ recovered from $F$ by clause (a) obey
$E=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$ and $B=\operatorname{curl}A$ with
$\varphi:=-cA_0$ and the spatial potential vector $A:=(A_1,A_2,A_3)$. Here
$\nabla$ and $\operatorname{curl}$ are those of

and the spatial cross-product conventions of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]] are
used. The definition does not assert that every field pair admits such a
potential; where a $C^1$ potential represents the $C^1$-or-better field of
clause (a), the field is closed in the explicit sense
$\partial_\lambda F_{\mu\nu}+\partial_\mu F_{\nu\lambda}
+\partial_\nu F_{\lambda\mu}=0$. This conclusion does not require second
classical derivatives of the potential: put
$H_{\lambda\mu\nu}:=\partial_\lambda F_{\mu\nu}+\partial_\mu F_{\nu\lambda}

([[lem-sr-compact-variation-and-fundamental-lemma]] (b)) and then off the

([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]), gives $\int H\psi=0$; the
fundamental lemma (a) of [[lem-sr-compact-variation-and-fundamental-lemma]]

([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), $c>0$, $m>0$, and let

([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]) in which a massive particle has
four-velocity $U=\gamma_w(c,w)$
([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]],
[[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(e)) with
$w=(3c/5,0,0)$, so that $\gamma_w=5/4$. Then its four-momentum is $P=mU$ with
components $(5mc/4,\,3mc/4,\,0,\,0)$. Relative to the stationary observer
$n=e_0$: $E_n(P)=5mc^2/4$, $q_n(P)$ has coordinates $(3mc/4,0,0)$, the
kinetic energy is $T_n(P)=mc^2/4$, and the mass shell
$E_n(P)^2-c^2|q_n(P)|^2=m^2c^4$ reads
$25m^2c^4/16-9m^2c^4/16=m^2c^4$. The exact kinetic energy
$mc^2/4=0.25\,mc^2$ exceeds the Newtonian expression
$\tfrac12m|w|^2=9mc^2/50=0.18\,mc^2$; the comparison is a numerical
specialisation, not a limiting claim and not a measurement.

[F1] ([[ex-sr-four-momentum-at-beta-three-fifths]], Example): in the original
frame $P=mU$ with $U=\gamma_w(c,w)$, $\gamma_w=5/4$, and $P$ has components
$(5mc/4,3mc/4,0,0)$, observer energy $5mc^2/4$ and spatial momentum
$(3mc/4,0,0)$.

[F2] ([[def-lorentz-boost]] and
[[lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse]]): the boost with parameter
$\beta=(v/c)s$, $|v|<c$, has $\gamma_v=(1-v^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$ and matrix
$B^0{}_0=\gamma_v$, $B^0{}_i=B^i{}_0=-\gamma_v(v/c)s_i$; it is a proper
orthochronous Lorentz map and is invertible.

[F3] ([[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]], clause (i)): under a
coordinate change $x'=\Lambda x+b$ the components of a vector transform as
$P'^a=\Lambda^a{}_bP^b$; applied to $\Lambda=B(\beta)$ this gives
$E'=\gamma_v(E-vp_\parallel)$, $p'_\parallel=\gamma_v(p_\parallel-vE/c^2)$,
$p'_\perp=p_\perp$ with $p_\parallel$ the component of $\mathbf p$ along $s$.

[F4] ([[lem-sr-four-momentum-in-inertial-frame]], clauses (a) and (c)): in an
inertial frame with stationary observer $e_0$ the components are
$(E_{e_0}(P)/c,q^1,q^2,q^3)$, and the combination
$E^2-c^2|\mathbf p|^2$ is invariant with value $m(P)^2c^4$ for future timelike
$P$.

[F5] ([[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]], Statement (b)): for
$P=mU$ with $m>0$, $U$ future timelike with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$, and $n$ future
unit, $T_n(P)=mc^2(\gamma-1)$ with $\gamma=-\eta(U/c,n)\ge1$, and
$T_n(P)=0$ if and only if $U=cn$.

The transition is $x'=B(\beta e_1)x$ with parameter $\beta e_1$ of modulus $|\beta|<1$, so [F2] clause (i) with $s=e_1$ gives the frame-$x'$ data $(\omega',s')$ of the same covector $k$ with $\omega'=\gamma_\beta(1-\beta)\omega$ and $\gamma_\beta=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$, this being the reading of the rest observer of $x'$ by clause (ii); and $\gamma_\beta(1-\beta)=(1-\beta)^{1/2}(1+\beta)^{-1/2}=((1-\beta)/(1+\beta))^{1/2}$ by [F8], the positive square root. Hence the dimensionless ratio $F(\beta):=\omega'/\omega$ equals $((1-\beta)/(1+\beta))^{1/2}$ for every $\beta\in(-1,1)$. [construct, A1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, F8]

exact_consumed_assertions: [L1] The transition of two inertial charts is affine with linear part $\Lambda=M^{-1}$, the matrix of the proper orthochronous linear Lorentz map $L$ with $Le_a=e'_a$; the linear parts of transitions are exactly the proper orthochronous Lorentz matrices and their inverses ([[lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz]]).

[L2] A linear Lorentz map is a linear isomorphism preserving $\eta$; its matrix in an orthonormal basis satisfies the metric condition; it is proper when its determinant is $+1$ and orthochronous when it maps $C^+$ onto $C^+$; the affine Lorentz maps form a group ([[def-lorentz-map-and-lorentz-group]], [[lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure]]).

[L3] A $\mathcal C^k$ type-$(r,s)$ tensor field on $\Omega$ assigns to $p\in\Omega$ a multilinear $T(p):(V^*)^r\times V^s\to\mathbb R$, with components $T^{a_1\dots a_r}{}_{b_1\dots b_s}(p)=T(p)(e^{*a_1},\dots,e_{b_1},\dots)$ in a frame, and regularity is chart-independent ([[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]], [[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]).

[L6] An alternating $k$-linear map is a $k$-linear map vanishing whenever two arguments coincide ([[def-alternating-k-linear-map]]); the oriented volume form of the model is $\epsilon(v_0,\dots,v_3)=\det([v_j^a])$ in an inertial frame, an alternating $4$-linear form with $\epsilon_{0123}=+1$ ([[def-oriented-minkowski-volume-form]]).

[L7] For a proper linear Lorentz map $L$ the oriented volume form satisfies $\epsilon(Lv_0,\dots,Lv_3)=\epsilon(v_0,\dots,v_3)$, and for $\det L=-1$ the two sides differ by the sign $-1$ ([[lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure]]).

[L8] At $\boldsymbol\beta=\mathbf0$ the boost is the identity; the quotient expressions in clause (vi) and the proof are used only for nonzero $\boldsymbol\beta$, with their spatial correction interpreted as zero at $\boldsymbol\beta=\mathbf0$. The passive boost with parameter $\boldsymbol\beta$ has the coordinate action and matrix displayed in [[def-lorentz-boost]], with inverse $B(-\boldsymbol\beta)$, and $\gamma=(1-|\boldsymbol\beta|^2)^{-1/2}$ ([[lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse]]).

2.2 For the covector field, write $k=k_b\,dx^b$ and $k=k'_a\,dx'^a$; since $x^c=(\Lambda^{-1})^c{}_a(x'^a-b^a)$, the chain rule [L12] gives $dx^c=(\Lambda^{-1})^c{}_a\,dx'^a$, so $k=k_b(\Lambda^{-1})^b{}_a\,dx'^a$ and comparing coefficients gives $k'_a=(\Lambda^{-1})^b{}_ak_b$. flat spacetime model of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]] and the SI unit
conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]], together with
the framework's idealisations of point particles, ideal clocks and ideal light
signals:

**(i) Mass and momentum.** Every massive classical particle of the model
carries a positive constant invariant mass parameter $m>0$ and has
four-momentum $P=mU$, where $U$ is the four-velocity of its future timelike
worldline ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]],
[[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]],
[[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]); $P$ is a vector of $V$
whose SI unit is kilogram metre per second. The formula is adopted only for
$m>0$; the case $m=0$ is not defined by it and is the separate premise
[[post-sr-ideal-massless-particle-momentum]]. In particular $\eta(P,P)=-m^2c^2$
is a consequence of the four-velocity normalisation, not a separate
assumption.

**(ii) Observer measurement identification.** Relative to a future unit
observer $n$, the model identifies the measured energy of the particle with
$E_n(P)$, its measured spatial momentum with $q_n(P)$, its kinetic energy with
$T_n(P)=E_n(P)-mc^2$ and its rest energy with $mc^2$, where $E_n,q_n,T_n$ are
the quantities of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]]; the
units are the joule, kilogram metre per second and kilogram of
[[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]. This clause is a formulation
convention identifying mathematical quantities with the quantities the model
calls measured; it is not a measurement report and no experiment is claimed.

**(iii) Isolated collision balance.** In an isolated collision of particles at
an event — the interaction being confined to that event, with no external
agent acting — the sum of the incoming four-momenta equals the sum of the
outgoing four-momenta, in the sense of the collision data of
[[def-sr-collision-datum-and-conservation]]: the model adopts
$Q_{\mathrm{in}}=Q_{\mathrm{out}}$ for such an isolated datum. No particular
collision is asserted to occur, and no mechanism, probability, cross section
or amplitude is supplied by this clause.

**(iv) Equation of motion for a stipulated force.** Whenever an interaction is
described by a stipulated force law $F$, that is a map assigning to an event
and a future timelike four-velocity a vector of $V$ on a stated domain, the
model's particle equation is $m\,dU/d\tau=F(x,U)$ along the worldline, with
$dU/d\tau$ the proper-time derivative of
[[def-sr-proper-time-derivative-and-four-force]], so that the stipulated $F$
is the four-force of the motion. A particular force law, and the existence,
uniqueness and domain of solutions of the resulting equation, are not adopted
here and belong to a separate model.

This remark delimits the interpretation of the proper-time comparison of the
twin reunion ([[texp-sr-piecewise-inertial-twin-reunion]]) in the adopted model, with the ideal clock assumptions of [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] and
[[post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis]] and the SI conventions of
[[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]. It proves nothing new; it
records what the earlier items do and do not assert.

In the model the reading of an ideal clock between two events of its history is
the proper-time integral of its worldline, by clause (i) of
[[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] for $C^1$ histories and by clause (ii) of
[[post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis]] for the weak piecewise $C^1$
class ([[def-sr-piecewise-proper-time]]); no term depending on the
four-acceleration ([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]) or on any
higher derivative of the history appears, and the clock hypothesis is precisely
the exclusion of such terms. The corner of the piecewise inertial history is an
idealization: a physical turnaround occupies a finite parameter interval, the
worldline is then $C^1$ or smooth there, and its proper time is still the
integral. The endpoint bound and strictness clause of
[[thm-sr-endpoint-proper-time-bound-and-flat-maximum]] apply to every weak
piecewise history, so the comparison with the stay-at-home clock survives the
smoothing of the corner, and the strict inequality remains because a smoothed
itinerary still does not have the image of the straight segment.

One history of the reunion is the straight segment from $p$ to $q$; the other
contains the corner event $r$ of [[texp-sr-piecewise-inertial-twin-reunion]], and
the three events $p,r,q$ are not collinear: in the chart of that item their
coordinate columns are $(0,0,0,0)$, $(cT,vT,0,0)$ and $(2cT,0,0,0)$ with
$vT\ne0$. Every change of inertial chart is an affine bijection
([[lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz]]) and maps collinear
triples to collinear triples, so no change of inertial frame maps the image of
the stay-at-home history onto the image of the traveler's history, nor fixes both
endpoints and exchanges the two histories. The two twins are therefore not
related by an inertial change of description, and the difference of readings is
a model consequence of the different histories, not a consequence of who is
'really moving': the symmetric time-dilation relation of
[[lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas]] (i) concerns the two frames,
while the reunion comparison concerns the two clock readings at the single
common event $q$.

In each momentary inertial rest frame of the traveler the stay-at-home clock runs
slow by the factor $1/\gamma$, and the traveler may legitimately apply the
time-dilation relation between events that are simultaneous in that momentary
frame ([[lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas]] (i),
[[def-sr-simultaneity-slice-and-rest-distance]]). But the two legs use different
inertial frames. With $\gamma=(1-v^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$ and the turn event $r$ of
[[texp-sr-piecewise-inertial-twin-reunion]], the outbound rest frame's chart
$x'$ satisfies $x'^0=\gamma\bigl(x^0-\frac vc x^1\bigr)$, so its slice through
$r$ has $x'^0=\gamma cT(1-v^2/c^2)=cT/\gamma$ and meets the stay-at-home
worldline $x^1=0$ at $x^0=\frac{1}{\gamma}\cdot\frac{cT}{\gamma}=cT(1-v^2/c^2)$,
that is at coordinate time $t=T(1-v^2/c^2)=T/\gamma^2$; the inbound rest frame's
chart $x''$ satisfies $x''^0=\gamma\bigl(x^0+\frac vc x^1\bigr)$, and its slice
through $r$ meets the same worldline at $x^0=cT(1+v^2/c^2)$, that is at
coordinate time $t=T(1+v^2/c^2)$. The two slices differ by
$2Tv^2/c^2$ in coordinate time, and the identity
$$2T=\frac{T}{\gamma^2}+\frac{2Tv^2}{c^2}+\frac{T}{\gamma^2},$$
which only uses $1/\gamma^2=1-v^2/c^2$, inserts this gap into the traveler's two
leg-by-leg accounts and reproduces the stay-at-home reading $2T$ at the reunion,
in agreement with the conditional comparison result
[[pthm-sr-same-endpoint-clock-comparison]]. The naive reciprocity statement
'each twin judges the other's clock to run slow' therefore compares different
pairs of events for the two travelers — events simultaneous in different
momentary frames — and does not apply to the reunion comparison, which concerns
the two clock readings at the single common event $q$.

Everything above is a conditional statement about ideal clocks in the adopted
model: the clocks are ideal with no acceleration-dependent reading term, the
histories are prescribed, spacetime is flat and $c$ is fixed
([[post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis]],
[[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]]). No measurement, apparatus, calibration,
sampling or uncertainty model is involved, and no claim is made about real
clocks or about nature; real clock comparisons would additionally require
apparatus and uncertainty analysis and are outside this remark.

Two events measured by the same observer are **radar-simultaneous** when their radar times agree. The assignment does not change under increasing reparametrizations of the observer's worldline, because the proper-time function does not ([[lem-sr-proper-time-reparametrization-invariance]]).

$$m:=\frac I2\int_0^L\gamma(s)\times\gamma'(s)\,ds,$$
again a componentwise Riemann integral over the compact interval $[0,L]$ of continuous functions; for the circle $\gamma(s)=a(\cos(s/a),\sin(s/a),0)$ traversed in the positive orientation this is $m=I\pi a^2e_3$.

**(c) [Status and scope].** In both clauses $m$ is a source moment of the declared current model: it is not a rest mass, not an intrinsic spin and not an observed quantity. The definition asserts no far-field property of $m$ (that is the content of [[pthm-em-magnetic-dipole-field]] under its hypotheses), no agreement between the two clauses in a common limit, and no moment for currents outside the two classes; no higher multipole is defined here. The finite Riemann moment definitions and circular-loop evaluation themselves are choice-free; no distribution-embedding or surface-measure theorem is used to compute these moments.

**Well-definedness and units.** In (a), $y\mapsto y\times J(y)$ is continuous on the compact rectangle $Q$ and vanishes off $\operatorname{supp}J$, so each component is Riemann integrable on $Q$ by [[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]] and bounded there, hence the integral of [[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]] is finite. Two bounding rectangles are compared through a common larger rectangle subdivided at their face coordinates: every added cell lies outside $\operatorname{supp}J$, where the integrand vanishes, so finite additivity of the integral ([[thm-multidimensional-integral-properties]]) identifies both values without integrating over the support itself. The cross product is that of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]. Since $y$ carries the metre and $J$ the ampere per square metre, the product $y\times J$ carries A m$^{-1}$ and the volume integral A m$^2$ ([[def-em-si-conventions]]). In (b), $\gamma$ and $\gamma'$ are continuous on the compact circle and periodic, so each component of $\gamma\times\gamma'$ is a continuous periodic function on $[0,L]$ and the componentwise Riemann integral exists; $|\gamma'|\equiv1$ makes the parametrization unit-speed so that the value is independent of an orientation-preserving change of unit-speed parameter; reversing orientation reverses the tangent current unless the signed current parameter $I$ is also reversed.
